chunks: As for what ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar narrated from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, he said:

I asked him about a man who plays with a woman and kisses her, then semen comes out from him—what is upon him? He said: “If desire came, and it gushed forth, and he experienced slackening upon its خروج, then ghusl is required upon him. But if it was only something for which he did not find any slackening nor desire, then there is no harm.”

His statement عليه السلام, “But if it was only something for which he did not find any slackening nor desire, then there is no harm,” means: if what came out was not the major fluid. For it is far-fetched in ordinary experience and human nature that semen should come out from a person while he finds from it neither desire nor pleasure. Rather, what is meant is that when the matter is doubtful to a person and he thinks that it is semen—while in reality it may not be semen—he evaluates it by the presence of desire within himself. So if he finds it, ghusl becomes obligatory upon him, and if he does not find it, he knows that what came out from him is not semen.

key_terms.الشَّهْوَةُ: sexual desire, a determining sign in identifying manī
key_terms.الْمَاءَ الْأَكْبَرَ: the major fluid, meaning semen in this context
key_terms.الْمَنِيُّ: semen, the discharge that entails ghusl when its signs are present
key_terms.دَفَقَ: gushed forth forcefully, indicating emitted semen
key_terms.فَتْرَةً: slackening or relaxation after emission, a legal sign mentioned in the ruling

ai.seo_question: When does discharge caused by intimacy require ghusl in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on when ghusl becomes obligatory after intimate play resulting in discharge. The criterion given is the presence of shahwah, forceful emission, and bodily slackening, while doubtful discharge without such signs is not treated as manī.
